'''Erich Peter Wohlfarth''' (7 December 1924 in [[Gliwice|Gleiwitz]], [[Upper Silesia]] – 16 March 1988, in London)  was a theoretical physicist.<ref name=":0" /> He is known for his work in [[magnetism]], in particular the [[Stoner–Wohlfarth model]] he developed together with his doctoral advisor and teacher, [[Edmund Clifton Stoner|E.C. Stoner]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1 June 1988 |title=Obituary: Professor E.P. Wohlfarth |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0304885388902818 |journal=Journal of Magnetism and Magnetic Materials |volume=73 |issue=2 |pages=i |doi=10.1016/0304-8853(88)90281-8 |bibcode=1988JMMM...73D...1. |issn=0304-8853|url-access=subscription }}</ref> The [[Institute of Physics]]' Magnetism Group's annual [[Wohlfarth Lectureship|Wohlfarth Memorial Lecture]] is named after him.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Erich Peter Wohlfarth and the Wohlfarth Lecture Series {{!}} Institute of Physics |url=https://www.iop.org/physics-community/special-interest-groups/magnetism-group/wohlfarth-lecture-series |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=www.iop.org |language=en}}</ref>

Wohlfarth's family emigrated from Germany to England in 1933 to escape political persecution.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Friedlaender |first1=F.J. |last2=Kneller |first2=E. |last3=Methfessel |first3=S. |last4=Wagner |first4=D. |year=1991 |title=Erich Peter Wohlfarth |journal=IEEE Transactions on Magnetics |volume=27 |issue=4 |pages=3469–3474 |doi=10.1109/TMAG.1991.1183749 |bibcode=1991ITM....27.3469F |issn=1941-0069}}</ref> He was educated at [[Bingley Grammar School]] and went on to study at the [[University of Leeds]], earning a BSc in physics in 1946, and a PhD in 1948 for work conducted under the supervision of [[E. C. Stoner (physicist)|E. C. Stoner]]. He was later awarded the D.Sc. degree in 1957, again by the [[University of Leeds]]. In 1948 he moved to [[Imperial College London]] to become a lecturer in the Department of Mathematics. In 1964, he was promoted to the position of Professor of Theoretical Magnetism.
